title: A tensor inverse detects a line module on an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$, with its small etale site and structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], chosen small relative to the sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $M,N$ be sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and use the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. If there exists an $\mathcal O_X$-linear isomorphism $M\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}N\cong\mathcal O_X$, then both $M$ and $N$ are locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X$ on the small etale site, hence are line modules. No finite-presentation hypothesis on $M$ or $N$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0B8N (lemma-invertible), equivalence (1)-(2), and Tag 0B8Q (lemma-invertible-is-locally-free-rank-1), locally ringed converse, applied to the small etale structure sheaf of an algebraic space.

proof.text: Fix an object $U\to X$ of the small etale site and write $\psi:M\otimes N\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_X$ for the given isomorphism. Work on localized sites. By the cited restriction theorem, for every object $W$ of the small etale site there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_W$-modules $(M\otimes N)|_W\cong M|_W\otimes_{\mathcal O_W}N|_W$, natural in $M,N$, sending the image of $x\otimes y$ under the sheafification unit on the original site to the image of $x\otimes y$ under the sheafification unit on the slice, for $x\in M(V)$, $y\in N(V)$, $V\to W$. Use this identification throughout, for $W=U$ and for the members of the coverings chosen below. In particular $\psi$ restricts to an isomorphism $M|_W\otimes_{\mathcal O_W}N|_W\cong\mathcal O_W$ on every slice, and a section of $M\otimes N$ that is the image of a pure tensor $x\otimes y$ corresponds on the slice to the image of the same pure tensor.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback) for the localization morphism of Section 03DH (section-localize)

proof.text: Apply local representability of sheafification sections to $t=\psi^{-1}(1)\in(M\otimes N)(U)$. The sheaf tensor is the abelian sheafification of $P(V)=M(V)\otimes_{\mathcal O_X(V)}N(V)$, with its extended module action; its underlying set sheaf is therefore the set sheafification of $|P|$. The cited local-sections theorem gives an etale covering on which $t$ comes from an element of this ordinary tensor product. Every ordinary tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors (expand its expression in the generators and absorb coefficients and minus signs into the first factor). Thus on each member $U_j$ of this covering there are sections $x_i\in M(U_j)$, $y_i\in N(U_j)$, $1\leq i\leq r$, with $t|_{U_j}=\sum_i x_i\otimes y_i$ (images under the sheafification unit). Renaming $U_j$ as $U$, we work on one member at a time; it suffices to trivialize $M$ and $N$ on a covering of each member. We may pad a zero expression by $0\otimes0$, so $r\geq1$. Applying $\psi$ gives $\sum_i\psi(x_i\otimes y_i)=1$.

source.place: Tag 0B8N (lemma-invertible), proof, local finite-sum representation; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules); Sites Tags 00YR and 00WK

proof.text: Put $a_i=\psi(x_i\otimes y_i)\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. At every point $u$ of the scheme $U$, its local ring cannot have all germs $(a_i)_u$ in its maximal ideal, since their sum is $1$. Choose an $i$ for which $(a_i)_u$ is a unit. Represent its inverse germ by a section $b$ on a Zariski neighbourhood; the germ equality $a_i b=1$ holds on a smaller neighbourhood, by the definition of a germ. These neighbourhoods, for all $u$, form a Zariski cover on which some $a_i$ is a unit. Their inclusions are etale, so they refine our covering in the small etale site. On any member replace $x_i$ by $a_i^{-1}x_i$ and denote the resulting pair by $x,y$. Then $\psi(x\otimes y)=1$, and injectivity of $\psi$ gives $\psi^{-1}(1)=x\otimes y$ on this slice. If $U$ is empty it is covered by the empty family, and there is nothing to check.

source.place: Tag 0B8Q (lemma-invertible-is-locally-free-rank-1), locally ringed converse; local-unit refinement written out on the scheme objects

proof.text: On this slice define $f:\mathcal O_U\to M|_U$ by $f(a)=ax$ and $g:M|_U\to\mathcal O_U$ by $g(m)=\psi(m\otimes y)$, on every object over $U$. These are module-sheaf maps because scalar multiplication and $\psi$ commute with restrictions, and $gf=\mathrm{id}$ since $\psi(x\otimes y)=1$. The endomorphism $T=fg$ of $M|_U$ is also an isomorphism: it is the composite $M\cong M\otimes\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{1\otimes\psi^{-1}}M\otimes(M\otimes N)\cong M\otimes(M\otimes N)\xrightarrow{1\otimes\psi}M\otimes\mathcal O_U\cong M$, where the middle isomorphism swaps the two $M$ factors using associativity and symmetry. Indeed its value on $m$ is $x\psi(m\otimes y)$, because $\psi^{-1}(1)=x\otimes y$. Every displayed arrow is an isomorphism by the cited monoidal structure and the hypothesis on $\psi$. Now $T^2=f(gf)g=fg=T$, and composing with $T^{-1}$ gives $T=\mathrm{id}$. Consequently $f,g$ are inverse trivializations of $M|_U$.

source.place: Tag 0B8N (lemma-invertible), proof, automorphism obtained by exchanging the two copies of the first tensor factor; idempotence for a single normalized pair

proof.text: For $N|_U$ use the isomorphism $\psi^{\mathrm{op}}:N\otimes M\xrightarrow{c}M\otimes N\xrightarrow{\psi}\mathcal O_U$ and the normalized pair $y,x$. Explicitly set $f_N(a)=ay$, $g_N(n)=\psi(x\otimes n)$. Then $g_Nf_N=\mathrm{id}$. The same displayed composite as in the previous step, with $N,M,\psi^{\mathrm{op}}$ substituted for $M,N,\psi$, is an isomorphism $T_N(n)=y\psi(x\otimes n)=f_Ng_N(n)$. Its square is itself since $g_Nf_N=\mathrm{id}$; hence it is the identity. These maps therefore trivialize $N$ on the same covering. Since the starting site object $U$ was arbitrary, both sheaves are locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_X$, which is precisely the definition of line modules. The construction never assumed finite presentation.
